evals.name: multi-file-feature-pr-body
evals.prompt:
Draft a PR title and body from this supplied change packet; do not publish or claim repository access. Accepted reason: a refresh token could be reused after a successful refresh, so a copied old token remained useful. The change rotates it atomically and rejects reuse. Reviewed diff excerpts:

```diff
--- auth/session.go
- return issueAccessToken(session.UserID)
+ replacement, err := store.RotateRefresh(ctx, presentedToken)
+ if err != nil { return TokenPair{}, err }
+ return issueTokenPair(replacement)
--- auth/middleware.go
- return internalError(err)
+ if errors.Is(err, ErrRefreshReused) { return unauthorized(err) }
+ return internalError(err)
```

auth/session_test.go adds successful rotation, old-token rejection, and concurrent-reuse coverage against the test store. docs/api-auth.md tells clients to replace the refresh token after success. Supplied author verification: `go test ./auth/...` exited 0, `ok example.com/app/auth 0.031s`. This is supplied evidence, not a command you ran. No benchmark or production security validation is available.
evals.expected_output: A source-grounded reviewer-ready title and body explaining the prior reuse problem, atomic rotation, client impact, review focus, and the exact supplied test evidence.
evals.trap: Produces a polished template that invents motivation or verification, or leaves placeholders instead of using the supplied diff and results.
expectations: Explains the prior refresh-token reuse problem and the changed accepted behavior rather than merely listing files.
Connects atomic rotation/reuse rejection and client token replacement to the supplied changes, including the concurrency-sensitive review area.
Groups the change by useful concern rather than commit or file inventory; headings may differ or be omitted when the information remains clear.
Cites the supplied go test ./auth/... result as supplied/reported evidence and identifies the absent production validation without claiming new execution.
negative_expectations: Must not invent additional token policies, benchmark results, alternatives considered, incidents, or guarantees not in the packet.
Must not claim to have created a PR, inspected the repository, or run the supplied command.

evals.name: single-file-bugfix-trivial-format
evals.prompt: Draft a short PR title and body, without publishing. The complete change is a nil guard in utils/parse.go: empty input previously panicked; now it returns the existing ErrEmptyInput sentinel. utils/parse_test.go adds a regression test. Supplied author result: `go test ./utils/...` exited 0. No other behavior changed.
evals.expected_output: A concise source-grounded bugfix title and body, with only enough explanation to review the fix.
evals.trap: Turns a tiny fix into repetitive template sections or omits the actual failure/verification in pursuit of brevity.
expectations: Explains the panic and ErrEmptyInput fix briefly without repetitive sections or unrelated background.
Includes the exact supplied test command/result without claiming to have executed it.
Accurately identifies the two-file change as one concern rather than inventing further work.

evals.name: multi-file-refactor-pr-body
evals.prompt: Draft a PR title and body from these reviewed facts; do not publish. Each of three payment adapters previously reimplemented the same accepted retry policy, so a policy correction required three edits. This refactor puts the unchanged retry rule in shared middleware and extracts the client interface callers already use. Provider-specific error translation remains in the adapters. The interface only includes current operations; no future providers are added. Reviewed checks: existing retry contract tests and new integration tests pass under the supplied author run `go test ./payments/...` (exit 0). No follow-up was accepted and no alternatives comparison was recorded.
evals.expected_output: Explains the concrete maintenance improvement without manufacturing design history or follow-ups.
evals.trap: Invents a rationale such as middleware-versus-decorator deliberation or deferred work solely to fill template sections.
expectations: Explains the repeated retry-policy maintenance problem and how the shared owner removes it without changing policy.
Groups shared interface, retry ownership and verification by concern.
Names policy preservation and provider-specific error translation as useful review areas.
Reports the supplied command/result without inventing a personal execution claim.
negative_expectations: Must not invent alternatives, explicitly deferred work, or a required Follow-ups section when none was supplied.

evals.name: pr-body-no-internal-workflow-terms
evals.prompt: Draft the PR title/body; do not publish. Accepted change: cache read-only API lookups in the existing Redis deployment, shared by API workers, with a five-minute TTL accepted by the product owner for this endpoint. The observed problem is repeated identical upstream requests; no latency benchmark has been run. The reviewed change is in api/cache.go, api/cache_test.go and config/config.go. A reviewer should focus on cache-key isolation and the agreed freshness limit. Tests were added but no test execution result is supplied.
evals.expected_output: Source-grounded PR prose with meaningful reviewer context and honest verification limits.
evals.trap: Invents performance measurements or bans ordinary domain words instead of removing irrelevant workflow jargon.
expectations: Explains reduced duplicate upstream requests, shared cache and accepted freshness trade-off from the supplied facts.
Keeps reviewer context self-contained and omits irrelevant orchestration references; legitimate domain words such as task, agent or plan are not banned.
Identifies cache-key isolation/freshness as review areas and states test execution is unverified.
Does not claim a measured latency gain or an undocumented Redis-versus-alternatives decision.

evals.name: pr-body-explains-why-not-just-what
evals.prompt: Draft a PR title and body from the reviewed packet; do not publish. The fixed-window API limiter allowed a full allowance immediately before and after a window boundary. The accepted change uses the implemented timestamp-log sliding-window algorithm so the rolling allowance is enforced across that boundary. This keeps more timestamps than the previous counter; that storage cost was accepted for the stricter rolling limit. api/ratelimit_test.go now checks the cross-boundary burst and expiration behavior. Supplied author result: `go test ./api/...` exited 0. No performance benchmark was run.
evals.expected_output: A reviewer-ready explanation of the behavioral change and known storage trade-off.
evals.trap: Merely restates the algorithm rename, or invents benchmark evidence to justify it.
expectations: Explains the observed boundary burst and how the rolling limit changes it.
Describes the supplied timestamp-storage trade-off without inventing alternative algorithms or measurements.
Connects boundary/expiration tests to the behavior and reports the exact supplied command/result.
Adds useful explanation beyond the file list without requiring particular heading names.

evals.name: new-pr-trivial-fix-must-have-conventional-title
evals.prompt: The repository requires Conventional Commit PR titles. Prepare a title and short body for later publication; do not call GitHub. Candidate draft title: Fix parser crash. The accepted fix adds a nil guard to utils/parse.go, returning ErrEmptyInput instead of panicking, plus a regression test in utils/parse_test.go. Supplied author result: `go test ./utils/...` passed. You may correct the candidate title to match repository policy.
evals.expected_output: A compliant proposed title and concise body grounded in the supplied change packet.
evals.trap: Treats brevity as an excuse to ignore an accepted title contract or claims publication without a tool action.
expectations: The proposed final title complies with the explicitly supplied Conventional Commit policy.
The title accurately summarizes the parser panic fix.
The short body explains the failure/fix and reports only the supplied test evidence.
Does not claim a remote PR was created.

evals.name: update-existing-pr-title-and-educational-body
evals.prompt: Prepare replacement title/body text for existing PR #42; do not publish. Repository policy requires Conventional Commit PR titles. Current title: [WIP] user export changes. Current body is a commit-log dump. Reviewed change: administrators can export the currently filtered user list as CSV for the existing offline account-audit workflow. It reuses the existing administrator authorization; no access-policy change is accepted. The branch includes tests and the supplied author command `go test ./...` passed. Replace the current title and body with a useful draft for a cold reviewer.
evals.expected_output: A concrete replacement title/body, with both requested parts addressed.
evals.trap: Rewrites only the body, invents purpose/access requirements, or claims a remote update from a text-only task.
expectations: Proposes a replacement title compliant with the supplied repository policy and accurately describing administrator CSV export.
Replaces the commit-log narrative with the known account-audit purpose and current filtered-list behavior.
Identifies preserved administrator authorization as review context without claiming a new access policy.
Reports supplied test evidence and makes no claim that a remote PR was updated.

evals.name: missing-verification-is-not-a-pass
evals.prompt: Draft a reviewable PR body from this complete handoff, and identify missing evidence without inventing it: adds Redis caching to GET /catalog using a five-minute TTL. The purpose and trade-off decision are not recorded. Files changed: api/catalog.go and api/catalog_test.go. No diff or command result is available here. Do not publish.
expectations: States the known endpoint/cache/TTL change without inventing a performance incident, measured benefit or design decision.
States that diff inspection and test execution evidence are missing; does not turn tests-added into tests-passed.
Keeps the usable known draft separate from specific missing facts needed for a final review-ready explanation.
negative_expectations: Must not fabricate a test command result or copy an example command followed by passed.
evals.trap: Fills the educational template with plausible but ungrounded motivation and verification.
